source.author: lucan
source.text: Propulit ut classem velis cedentibus Auster Incumbens, mediumque rates movere profundum, Omnis in Ionios spectabat navita fluctus: Solus ab Hesperia non flexit lumina terra Magnus, dum patrios portus, dum litora numquam Ad visus reditura suos, tectumque cacumen Nubibus, et dubios cernit vanescere montes.
source.text_original: Propulit ut classem velis cedentibus Auster / Incumbens, mediumque rates movere profundum, / Omnis in Ionios spectabat navita fluctus: / Solus ab Hesperia non flexit lumina terra / Magnus, dum patrios portus, dum litora numquam / Ad visus reditura suos, tectumque cacumen / Nubibus, et dubios cernit vanescere montes.
source.text_english: When Auster, pressing with yielding sails, had driven the fleet forward and the ships were moving through the middle of the deep, every sailor was looking toward the Ionian waves; Magnus alone did not turn his eyes from the Hesperian land, while he saw the native harbors, while he saw the shores that would never return to his sight, and the mountain peak hidden by clouds and the wavering mountains fading from view.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Interea medio saevus permissa profundo carbasa Pangaea Boreas speculatus ab arce continuo Aeoliam Tyrrhenaque tendit ad antra concitus.
reuse.text_original: Interea medio saevus permissa profundo / carbasa Pangaea Boreas speculatus ab arce / continuo Aeoliam Tyrrhenaque tendit ad antra / concitus.
reuse.text_english: Meanwhile, from the Pangaean citadel, fierce Boreas, having surveyed the sails entrusted to the deep in mid-ocean, at once, roused, speeds toward Aeolia and the Tyrrhenian caves.
